sentences.text: 1. Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 02.02.2022 passed in MVC.No.3646/2018 by XX Additional Small Causes Judge and Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate and MACT, Bengaluru (for short 'Tribunal'), the respondent therein has preferred MFA.No.336/2020 and the petitioners therein have preferred MFA.crob.No.139/2022.

entities.text: Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate and MACT, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that, on 22.05.2018 at about 12.30 p.m., the petitioner was riding motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-04-EQ-1830 from Madanapalli to Hulyurdurga and when he reached near Beechanahalli, at that time, a KSRTC bus bearing registration No. KA-11-F- 0059 being driven in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the motor cycle and the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
i. Fracture of both bones of right leg.
ii. Fracture of right femur.
4.
The petitioner was aged about 12 years at the time of the accident.
He preferred MVC.No.3646/2018 and the Tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs.3,22,000/- along with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of petition till the date of realization.

Aggrieved by the same, the respondent has preferred MFA.No.3366/2021 and not satisfied by the compensation awarded, the petitioner has preferred MFA.CROB.No.139/2022.
5.
The case of the respondent is that the accident happened due to rash and negligent driving of the motor cycle and not by the driver of the KSRTC bus.

The rider of the bike was a minor and did not have valid driving license.
6.

With regard to the contention that the accident happened due to rash and negligent driving of the driver, the respondents have examined the conductor, who has said that seeing the motor cycle, the driver of the bus stopped about 70 feet away from the motor cycle, but the motor cycle itself came and dashed against the bus.
However, the seizure mahazar at Ex.P3 records it otherwise and FIR and charge sheet are filed against the driver of the bus.
The trial Court based on the evidence available has held that the accident was caused by negligence of the driver of the bus.
I do not see any reason why this Court has to interfere with the finding of the Tribunal in this regard.

However,
it is needless to state that this will not come in the way of the driver defending the case otherwise before the criminal court and criminal court has to take the decision based on the evidence adduced before it.

3 7.
With regard to the contention that the rider of the bike was a minor, the respondent has failed to take such a contention before the Tribunal.
No issues have been framed regarding the same nor any evidence is let in regarding the same and the contention of the respondent in this regard now is not acceptable.

However, it is needless to state that the driving of a vehicle by a minor or by a person without valid driving license will be viewed seriously by courts and it is to be considered negligent act on part of such drivers.
Similarly, if a vehicle is to be driven without due insurance that also will be taken seriously by the courts.
However, mere allegation without any evidence to that effect is not sufficient.
The same has to be pleaded and proved before the Tribunal, which has not been done in the instant case.
8. For the aforementioned reasons, the appeal filed by the respondent deserves to be dismissed.

9. In respect of MFA.CROB.No.139/2022 for enhancement of the compensation, it is seen that the petitioner is a minor and as per the doctor's evidence he has suffered multiple fractures in his right lower limb and there is 37% disability to the right lower limb.
The doctor however says that there is total body disability of 19%.

But the doctor's evidence is not clear that how he has arrived at the total body disability at 19% and the Tribunal based upon the judgment in Master Mallikarjun Vs Divisional Manager, The National Insurance company Limited and another reported in ILR 2013 Karnataka 4891 (SC) has come to the conclusion as there is a total body disability between 10% to 30%, the petitioner deserved to be awarded a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- towards the 'Pain and suffering'
and accordingly has awarded the same.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun Vs Divisional Manager, The National Insurance company Limited and another reported in ILR 2013 Karnataka 4891 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, another sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under the head of discomfort, inconvenience and loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization and Rs.1,353.57/- towards 'Medical expenses', based on the actual bills and has rounded off the compensation amount to Rs.3,22,000/-.
The petitioner is not in a position to state as to how the order of the Tribunal is erroneous and on what count additional compensation has to be awarded to him.
I find the order of the Tribunal to be just fair and reasonable.
For the said reason, the appeal filed by the petitioners also deserves to be dismissed.

10. Hence, the following;
ORDER i. MFA.No.3366/2021 filed by respondent - KSRTC is dismissed.
ii. MFA.CROB.No.139/2022 filed by the claimants is dismissed.
iii. Registry is directed to send the records to the concerned jurisdictional Tribunal forthwith.
Amount-in-deposit, if any, before this Court shall be transferred to the concerned MACT for disbursement.
